sources.title: Guarani Ñandeva
sources.note: Instituto Socioambiental synthesis of tekoha as land, forest, water, plants, remedies, extended-family relations, and specific historical attachment rather than abstract territory.

sources.title: Guarani Kaiowá
sources.note: Institutional synthesis distinguishing Ñandeva, Kaiowa, and Mbyá language, custom, ritual, social organization, religion, and historical experience.

sources.title: Guarani Mbyá
sources.note: Institutional synthesis of Mbyá settlement, kinship, reciprocity, mobility, forest, farming, water, and spiritual leadership, used with explicit modern and subgroup scope.

sources.title: Guarani Mbyá language identification
sources.note: Brazilian cultural heritage inventory identifying Mbyá as one Guarani language reference alongside Ñandeva, Avá, and Kaiowa.

sources.title: Paraguay National Plan for Indigenous Peoples
sources.note: Official plan explaining territory as geographic, spiritual, cultural, historical, and practical, and quoting the Guarani point that land becomes tekoha through community presence and practice.

sources.title: Recovery of vernacular Guarani architecture
sources.note: Paraguayan CONACYT-supported study of tekoha, built space, forests, domestic structures, collective places, and historically specific Guarani architecture.

sources.title: Archaeological heritage of Paraná
sources.note: IPHAN overview of eight-thousand-year lithic sites, two-thousand-year ceramic horticultural sites, rock art, and later colonial contexts in Paraná.

sources.title: Tupiguarani potters, volume one
sources.note: IPHAN-hosted regional syntheses emphasizing variation in pottery and archaeological traditions across Brazil, Argentina, and adjacent regions.

sources.title: A model of regional Guarani occupation in southern Brazil
sources.note: University of São Paulo journal study of settlement distribution, site structure, artifacts, social networks, intercultural contact, and varied environmental zones around Laguna dos Patos.

sources.title: Regional organization of Guarani settlements
sources.note: Peer-reviewed ceramic analysis across eleven sites in the Taquari-Antas basin used to show regional settlement organization and variability.

sources.title: Guarani archaeology at the Célia Maria site
sources.note: Dated precolonial São Paulo site and reconstruction of pottery-making gestures and vessel forms from analyzed rim fragments.

sources.title: An ethnoarchaeological view of Guarani occupation in São Paulo
sources.note: Peer-reviewed discussion of black-earth house traces, settlements, fertile soil, water, fishing, hunting, forest agriculture, and the limits of ethnographic analogy.

sources.title: Functional taxonomy and plant microremains in Guarani vessels
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Misiones study of vessel forms, phytoliths, maize and squash starch, storage, cooking, serving, and analogy limits.

sources.title: Daily life in the Taquari Valley through pottery
sources.note: University journal study reconstructing seventy-two vessels used for cooking, storing, serving, eating, and drinking at one southern Brazilian site.

sources.title: Guarani populations in Santa Catarina
sources.note: Federal university museum account placing Guarani arrival on the Santa Catarina coast around 1000 CE and presenting archaeological materials as regional evidence.

sources.title: A model for Guarani expansion in the La Plata Basin
sources.note: University repository record for a radiocarbon and thermoluminescence synthesis of geographic and temporal site distribution.

sources.title: Archaeology at Iguazú Falls
sources.note: Peer-reviewed systematic survey of Iguazú National Park finding lithic-only contexts, Guarani pottery contexts, and radiocarbon dates.

sources.title: Arenal Central and Guarani occupation of the Paraná Delta
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis of a southern-edge residential site, chronology, subsistence, ceramics, burials, mobility, and evidence limits.

sources.title: Guarani pottery beyond rigid norms
sources.note: Peer-reviewed ethnoarchaeological discussion of Guarani pottery made by women, variation, technical choices, and the limits of rigid ceramic norms.

sources.title: Archaeology of fermented drinks among Tupi-Guarani peoples
sources.note: Peer-reviewed analysis of fermented beverages, vessel forms, social practice, and the danger of treating broad archaeological style as uniform society.

sources.title: Current Mbyá-Guarani medicinal plant exchanges
sources.note: Community-participatory study in seven southern Brazilian territories documenting plant exchanges and the relation among forest, health, education, knowledge, and culture.

sources.title: Childhood and teaching among Guarani Mbyá
sources.note: Ethnomusicological research showing children as learners and teachers through music and play in a specific modern Mbyá setting.

sources.title: Between song and pen: Guarani Mbyá knowledge
sources.note: Peer-reviewed research with Mbyá participants treating oral and written practice within broader production, acquisition, and transmission of knowledge.

sources.title: Guarani Mbyá children and Indigenous education centers
sources.note: Research on Mbyá educators, children, memory, oral knowledge, identity, and modern Indigenous early education in São Paulo.

sources.title: Housing, water, and sanitation in a Guarani birth cohort
sources.note: Modern study across sixty-three Guarani villages recording substantial diversity in water sources, toilets, waste removal, housing, and child environments.

sources.title: Ruiz de Montoya works reissued
sources.note: Paraguay cultural ministry account dating Montoya’s Guarani dictionary to 1639 and grammar and bilingual catechism to 1640, well after this card.

sources.title: Guarani Language Academy
sources.note: Paraguay language authority explaining present orthographic, lexical, grammatical, and community-sovereignty work and the modern official alphabet.

sources.title: Brazilian archaeological heritage
sources.note: Official explanation of archaeological stewardship, protected sites, pottery, tools, adornment, and the public duty to preserve contexts.

sources.title: Guarani presence in present-day Uruguay
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis stressing scattered, fragmentary, and unevenly contextualized evidence for Guarani presence in Uruguay.

sources.title: Construction of Guarani archaeological unity at its southern limit
sources.note: CONICET study of how archaeologists constructed a Guarani unit and the similarities and differences within southern evidence.

sources.title: When everyone becomes Guarani
sources.note: University dissertation showing how sixteenth-century writings generalized diverse peoples into a broad, homogeneous Guarani category.

sources.title: Practices and knowledge of tereré and pohã ñana
sources.note: UNESCO documentation of a living Paraguayan practice involving medicinal herbs, social transmission, and Guarani language, included only as later continuity.

sources.title: Arete Guasu and Indigenous-language documentation
sources.note: UNESCO account of living Guarani celebration, community-produced language documentation, ancestry, renewal, and cultural continuity in specific Paraguayan communities.

sources.title: Plant foods and landscapes in southern Brazil
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis of maize, manioc, beans, starch residues, settlement change, and cautions around archaeological cultural labels.

sources.title: Guarani archaeology on the southern Santa Catarina coast
sources.note: Peer-reviewed regional study of settlements among rivers, dunes, lagoons, and the Atlantic coast.

sources.title: Archaeometry of Guarani pottery in southern Brazil
sources.note: University journal study using X-ray fluorescence to test pottery composition and question purely visual classifications.

proposedOverrides.name: Tekohá (Guarani)
proposedOverrides.summary: A regional guide that corrects one oversized atlas polygon while respecting distinct Guarani peoples, tekoha, evidence, and continuity.
